subject: ADR-202: a check nobody can afford is a check that does not run -- the CI path filter, held to what the build actually reads
body: The CI workflow rebuilt the Java tree on two JDKs for EVERY PUSH TO EVERY BRANCH, and the last dozen slices are harness and page work containing no Java at all -- so the minutes went on rebuilding a tree nothing in them had changed, and ran out, which turns the check DARK on the pushes that do touch the build. A green history that means 'did not run' is worse than a red one. The fix is on.push.paths and on.pull_request.paths, the same list in both. It buys minutes at the cost of a guarantee: A FILTER THAT DOES NOT COVER A FILE THE BUILD READS MAKES THE BUILD SKIP A CHANGE THAT COULD BREAK IT, AND NOTHING SAYS SO. So the filter is not a setting, it is a CLAIM ABOUT THE BUILD and it is held to the build: verify_ci walks the tree, collects every file Gradle compiles, packages or is configured by, and fails if one falls outside. AN ALLOW-LIST, NOT A DENY-LIST -- a module added tomorrow lands under **/*.java and **/src/** on the day it appears, where a deny-list would silently stop covering it. THE WORKFLOW IS INSIDE ITS OWN FILTER, because a change to the build's definition that does not run the build cannot be told from one that skipped it on purpose. THE MATCHER IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART and it is approximate: `**` is consumed before `*`, or the second star reads as a separate single-segment wildcard and a pattern that looks right quietly stops matching across directories; and a pattern out of scope is REFUSED rather than treated as covering everything, because a matcher that answered yes to a pattern it had not understood would hold the filter to nothing while reporting that it held. The other direction is checked too: the files the last dozen slices actually changed must NOT match, or the filter is a filter in name only. verify_ci is NEW at 12 checks, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX and failing 7/11 against the unfiltered workflow; mutate_ci is NEW at 10 mutants all killed, each coverage pattern dropped from BOTH lists because the filter is written once and copied, plus three against the matcher itself. NOT FIXED: the minutes already spent -- until the quota resets the check is dark on every push; and A PATH FILTER ON A REQUIRED STATUS CHECK IS A TRAP, since a pull request touching no Java would never run a required `ci` and would sit pending forever. This repo pushes straight to main and has no required checks, so the trap is not sprung; it is written down because the next person to add branch protection will not otherwise know. ONE MORE THING THE BRIDGE DECIDED: the delivery bridge REFUSES to write .github/workflows -- writing a CI definition onto somebody's machine from a remote tool is a supply-chain hole, and the refusal is right -- so the workflow travels as tools/ci/ci.yml and is copied into place by the same command that pushes the slice. Two copies of one file drift, so verify_ci fails if they are not byte-identical, and mutate_ci has a mutant that drifts them.
